core_job: For someone going to stay in a country whose language they don't speak (one of 12 languages): translate what they need to say by typing or speaking, keep it, and practise saying it out loud until they can say it without the phone. Today the translator works through MyMemory (I checked it with curl and got HTTP 200), and Practice and the SM-2 flashcards also work. But nothing is remembered except bookmarks, bookmarks never become practice, and Chinese and Japanese practice cannot score correctly because the matcher splits on whitespace.
signature: The Say-it-back deck. Every saved translation becomes a spaced-repetition card. A review works like this: Hear it plays the phrase in the target language (system TTS, normal or slow speed), Say it listens with the phone's speech recogniser in that language, and the screen highlights the words or characters it heard. For Chinese and Japanese the match is counted per character. The app proposes a grade from the match (80% or more is Good, 50-79% is Hard, under 50% is Again) and the user can change it with one tap. The next due date comes from the SM-2 scheduling the app already has. If the phone has no recogniser for the language, the user grades themselves. Show it puts the phrase in large type for the other person to read. Reminders fire only when cards are actually due and state the real count. Everything runs on the device; the translation itself is the only network call.
must: M1 Phrase desk home, with no bottom NavigationBar and no 3-mode tabs. It has a language-pair bar saved from onboarding, typing and dictation, Hear it / Copy / Save to deck / Show it, a 'Due today · N' strip and Recent. Face to face is a full-screen split with the top half rotated 180°. Every translation is kept in history (verba.history.v1, cap 500, survives a restart).

M2 Say-it-back deck as specified in §3. PhraseMatch counts per character for zh and ja and per word for other languages. srs.dart holds SM-2 plus gradeFor thresholds. The Review screen has Hear it, Say it, highlighted matches, the proposed grade with an override, and self-grading when there is no recogniser. One deck store, verba.deck.v1, with a one-time migration from saved_phrases_v1 and flashcard_progress_v1 that keeps SM-2 state. Reminders only when cards are due, with the real count.

M3 Depth: History search, language-pair filter and swipe-delete with undo. Deck search with filters All / Due now / Struggling / Starter / Mine. CSV export of the deck through share_plus. An offline message inside the screen replaces the global OfflineBanner; deck, history, review and Show it still work offline. A specific message when MyMemory reports quotaFinished. A real empty state for each screen.
